Sentence (English): I really liked this dishwasher, and bought it because it was one of the 3 highest rated on Lowe's.
Comments (English): [ Worked great until it didn't ] || ---------------- || I really liked this dishwasher, and bought it because it was one of the 3 highest rated on Lowe's. After a little over a year of owning it, we started to get a drainage every now and then, which became more frequent. I took it apart to check for any clogs and didn't see anything. We would give it time and run it again without problems. They kept becoming more frequent, and I read online that it can be a motherboard issue, especially with this model. The easy fix is to unplug or turn off the circuit depending on how you wired it. This seemed to solve the problem for about another month. Now it runs a whole cycle, but doesn't circulate water. Either the motherboard is garbage or the circulation pump is shot. If I replace either one, I'm looking at a few hundred bucks, and if I pick wrong, it's more than the dishwasher costs to replace. If I pay a service tech to fix, it's going to be more than the dishwasher. I gave it 2 stars because it did an amazing job washing dishes when it worked. Sentence (English): The dishwasher does an excellent job of cleaning dishes and is exceedingly quiet.
Comments (English): [ Falls Short of Expectations ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher does an excellent job of cleaning dishes and is exceedingly quiet. My wife loves it - me, not so much. There are two aspects of the design that cause me to question how well this appliance will hold up over time. First, the door is very lightly constructed and can be easily torqued out of square with even a gentle pressure. Secondly, the roller mechanism for the racks feels cheap, sloppy and flimsy. Our children have long since left the house which, for this dishwasher, is a good thing. I think it would experience a lot failures with the rack slides and door seal if our kids were using it. Additionally, I find the racking for dishes to be "too clever by half". It appears to offer great flexibility, but in practice, I have to stuff bowls in odd places because the locations best suited to them fill up so quickly. As an aside, this is our second Bosch diswasher. The first one was certainly long-lived, but suffered from a recurring failure of the10 Amp heater power connection soldered directly to the PCB; a really crappy practice for that much current. The power was then switched by a 10 amp (maxium) relay. Unsurprisingly, that failed too. I can only hope that we're not going run into those sorts of cheesy cost-cutting measures with our new Bosch.

There are two aspects of the design that cause me to question how well this appliance will hold up over time. First, the door is very lightly constructed and can be easily torqued out of square with even a gentle pressure. Secondly, the roller mechanism for the racks feels cheap, sloppy and flimsy. Our children have long since left the house which, for this dishwasher, is a good thing. I think it would experience a lot failures with the rack slides and door seal if our kids were using it. Additionally, I find the racking for dishes to be "too clever by half". It appears to offer great flexibility, but in practice, I have to stuff bowls in odd places because the locations best suited to them fill up so quickly. As an aside, this is our second Bosch diswasher. The first one was certainly long-lived, but suffered from a recurring failure of the10 Amp heater power connection soldered directly to the PCB; a really crappy practice for that much current. The power was then switched by a 10 amp (maxium) relay. Unsurprisingly, that failed too. I can only hope that we're not going run into those sorts of cheesy cost-cutting measures with our new Bosch.

Comments (English): [ Great overall value ] || ---------------- || Our old (different brand) unit died on us, and being a first time homeowner and knowing nothing about this stuff, I started my research. After doing some due diligence in my research, and going to look at products over a few months, we landed on the GE over all the other brands. One thing I noted immediately was build quality in comparison to the rivals, who are typically electronics makers. Their construction didn't feel as solid or sturdy as the GE did. A few take always:The extra flatware row up top is a new feature for us that we are enjoying and still playing with. It's also convenient to have the ability to adjust the (formerly top rack) cup rack up and down etc. to help make all the things fit both above and below. This level also has a bottle blaster row that has larger prongs that have water jets in them to clean out your reusable bottles or those hard to reach locations. Super handy for those with kids or who like to use the reusable water bottles. It's SUPER SUPER quiet; I didn't measure against what GE states the decibel (db) level to be, but in my experience assisting in undersea acoustics in a past life, I believe this to be very close, if not quieter then the stated db level (I think their number was conservative). The bottom row has multiple adjustment points within the rack to change the configuration of the rows. I really like that feature as it changes how things fit - for the better! The instructions are extremely helpful in relaying all info, including the discrete details. As mentioned above I'm new to this and have never installed a DW! Small related sidebar - I read a review about this product where the person said after they installed it, that it was too loud. But I noted 2 locations in the instructions that called out specific steps to take to reduce noise levels and the reviewer in that instance stated they didn't complete one of the tasks. In that case it was user error, all they had to do was follow the well laid out instructions. That all to say, this puppy noise dampens well. I also like that it has a small convenience light on the front panel to indicate its status to you, so you know when it's running or complete - you're covered there too! I'm really enjoying the top buttons compared to the old front buttons. With the front buttons my kids press them because they make noise and light up, and so does my stomach or my belt, if I'm reaching for something in the cabinet etc. But with top buttons they are tucked up under the counter and even small wondering fingers can't make their way onto them (or my stomach)! In comparison to our old unit, this GE is night and day difference. And it brings a little peace of mind with the quality build and the GE name! A few improvements that could be made. Let's face it, what's an honest critique if we don't find something that can be done better? Something can ALWAYS be improved upon (the principal of continuous improvement)! Between the old unit and this one we lost some space inside for dishes and maybe silverware (yet to be seen as you can cover down on the new top row with some of the flatware). That removal of extra wash space however is likely what makes them more every efficient etc. I actually don't mind the loss of a small amount of the interior space as we tend to over pack these things anyway. I have no other suggested or recommended improvements and I have no other "complaints". I installed the unit with no issue as a first timer and needed zero help. I am only slightly mechanically inclined and was able to do this all in about 4 hours start to finish. It's also a looker! Looks great in place, we selected the stainless steel and love the look. Picture included.

After doing some due diligence in my research, and going to look at products over a few months, we landed on the GE over all the other brands. One thing I noted immediately was build quality in comparison to the rivals, who are typically electronics makers. Their construction didn't feel as solid or sturdy as the GE did. A few take always:The extra flatware row up top is a new feature for us that we are enjoying and still playing with. It's also convenient to have the ability to adjust the (formerly top rack) cup rack up and down etc. to help make all the things fit both above and below. This level also has a bottle blaster row that has larger prongs that have water jets in them to clean out your reusable bottles or those hard to reach locations. Super handy for those with kids or who like to use the reusable water bottles. It's SUPER SUPER quiet; I didn't measure against what GE states the decibel (db) level to be, but in my experience assisting in undersea acoustics in a past life, I believe this to be very close, if not quieter then the stated db level (I think their number was conservative). The bottom row has multiple adjustment points within the rack to change the configuration of the rows. I really like that feature as it changes how things fit - for the better! The instructions are extremely helpful in relaying all info, including the discrete details. As mentioned above I'm new to this and have never installed a DW! Small related sidebar - I read a review about this product where the person said after they installed it, that it was too loud. But I noted 2 locations in the instructions that called out specific steps to take to reduce noise levels and the reviewer in that instance stated they didn't complete one of the tasks. In that case it was user error, all they had to do was follow the well laid out instructions. That all to say, this puppy noise dampens well. I also like that it has a small convenience light on the front panel to indicate its status to you, so you know when it's running or complete - you're covered there too! I'm really enjoying the top buttons compared to the old front buttons. With the front buttons my kids press them because they make noise and light up, and so does my stomach or my belt, if I'm reaching for something in the cabinet etc. But with top buttons they are tucked up under the counter and even small wondering fingers can't make their way onto them (or my stomach)! In comparison to our old unit, this GE is night and day difference. And it brings a little peace of mind with the quality build and the GE name! A few improvements that could be made. Let's face it, what's an honest critique if we don't find something that can be done better? Something can ALWAYS be improved upon (the principal of continuous improvement)! Between the old unit and this one we lost some space inside for dishes and maybe silverware (yet to be seen as you can cover down on the new top row with some of the flatware). That removal of extra wash space however is likely what makes them more every efficient etc. I actually don't mind the loss of a small amount of the interior space as we tend to over pack these things anyway. I have no other suggested or recommended improvements and I have no other "complaints". I installed the unit with no issue as a first timer and needed zero help. I am only slightly mechanically inclined and was able to do this all in about 4 hours start to finish. It's also a looker! Looks great in place, we selected the stainless steel and love the look. Picture included.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher does an excellent job of cleaning dishes and is exceedingly quiet.
Comments (English): [ Falls Short of Expectations ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher does an excellent job of cleaning dishes and is exceedingly quiet. My wife loves it - me, not so much. There are two aspects of the design that cause me to question how well this appliance will hold up over time. First, the door is very lightly constructed and can be easily torqued out of square with even a gentle pressure. Secondly, the roller mechanism for the racks feels cheap, sloppy and flimsy. Our children have long since left the house which, for this dishwasher, is a good thing. I think it would experience a lot failures with the rack slides and door seal if our kids were using it. Additionally, I find the racking for dishes to be "too clever by half". It appears to offer great flexibility, but in practice, I have to stuff bowls in odd places because the locations best suited to them fill up so quickly.As an aside, this is our second Bosch diswasher. The first one was certainly long-lived, but suffered from a recurring failure of the10 Amp heater power connection soldered directly to the PCB; a really crappy practice for that much current. The power was then switched by a 10 amp (maxium) relay. Unsurprisingly, that failed too. I can only hope that we're not going run into those sorts of cheesy cost-cutting measures with our new Bosch.

Comments (English): [ It Has One Job and It's Terrible At It ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher replaced an older Kenmore one. For pros, it is very quiet, and I appreciate that it sort of sings at you when it's done and it opens the door a bit when it's finished to help air dry the dishes I guess. As for cleaning (it's one job), I do not know exactly why we have had such a rotten time with it when there are so many glowing reviews, but we desperately miss our old Kenmore. It does not consistently clean anything for us except silverware that we put in the top tray. At first when we were having issues I meticulously went through the manual to make sure we were placing dishes correctly. We made adjustments to how we handled pans in particular since we had been placing them incorrectly, but it did not help. Almost every time we run it we have to take items out and hand wash them or leave them for a second run. It's unclear why we even have this appliance at this point and we're seriously considering donating it and getting something else if we can scrape together the money.

Sentence (English): I got this for my washing machine so that I could have it run during non-peak hours but finish right when I have to wake up, so that I can move it to the dryer and not have it sit wet all night.
Comments (English): [ Works great after some troubleshooting ] || ---------------- || I got this for my washing machine so that I could have it run during non-peak hours but finish right when I have to wake up, so that I can move it to the dryer and not have it sit wet all night. It is working great for that so far! At first, I was having trouble getting it to connect like other reviewers were mentioning. What helped me was making sure that the door to the washing machine is closed. I usually have it open so that it can air out, but the smart control won't connect unless the door is closed and can be locked (that makes sense now as a safety feature, but it isn't mentioned in the instructions, so I'm guessing that may be where a lot of people are having issues). I also followed the advice from the other review that said "when the app prompts to quickly press the smart control button, hold it down until the machine gets out of the ap mode and then hold the button down again and put the machine in the ap mode again." Hopefully this helps other people who had issues!

Sentence (English): Before buying a dishwasher, I compared manufacturers from several different companies.
Comments (English): [ LG is the answer when it comes to dishwashers! ] || ---------------- || Before buying a dishwasher, I compared manufacturers from several different companies. I did a lot of comparisons on YouTube. I'm a firm believer in LG for home appliances, so I looked at LG products first. Then I looked at Samsung, and then SK, which seemed to have a good position in the dishwasher market, so I looked into that too. Although I haven't used either Samsung or SK, I'm quite satisfied with the LG dishwasher. The technician came and installed it, and I used it that evening, and, as expected from the reviews, there wasn't even a single water stain. I also purchased one with Wi-Fi. I thought it would be really convenient to be able to control it via mobile and have it send status updates. Thanks to Coupang, I think I made a good, cost-effective purchase. Sentence (English): We have had this dishwasher about 3 months and use it almost once per day.
Comments (English): [ Great so far, there are minor changes I would make ] || ---------------- || We have had this dishwasher about 3 months and use it almost once per day. We are first time homeowners and having only had economy dishwashers in our rentals, we decided to splurge a little on a new dishwasher selecting this one over the other lower models. I like that this model has a stainless steel inner tub (seems like plastic tub models develop an odor over time), advertised to be quieter than the lower models, has a 3rd rack, heated dry, top controls, and 2 handle variations to match other appliances. Now that we have had some time to use it I find that our dishes come out clean, it doesn't seem to use too much rinse aid, it is very quiet during the wash cycle (loud at times during draining but it's honestly nothing to complain about), and has lots of room for our dishes especially with the lower utensil basket removed. I appreciate being able to see an estimated cycle time based on cycle selection and remaining time on the display. The led indicator on the front is very helpful and not obnoxiously bright. Blue for cleaning, red during drying, white when done. Also, the “Clean” indicator does not cancel when the door is opened, only when latched and opened again. I pop the door open to let dishes continue air drying and with the clean indicator remaining on allows other members of our household to see the status. I'll be curious to see how this dishwasher lasts in general. Nothing seems to last anymore. To Whirlpool: There are a couple of small changes I would suggest for future iterations of this model- I frequently cancel the heated dry most times to save energy. I find that the dishes are adequately dry without heated dry AND leaving the door cracked for a little while following a wash cycle. That said, an “Eco” cycle/button would be a great addition. The front handle really flexes the door when having to yank the door open. I love how tight the door closes and seals so perhaps some added structure to the front door would help it feel more sturdy. The top silverware rack is pretty good but other competing dishwashers have a more simple rack to accommodate silverware more universally. Some of our silverware fits the profile, some not quite. Lastly, I haven't looked very closely so if this is possible, please disregard. but it would be nice to be able to remove the top utensil rack for loads with taller dishes in the top rack, as an option.

One thing I noted immediately was build quality in comparison to the rivals, who are typically electronics makers. Their construction didn't feel as solid or sturdy as the GE did. A few take always: The extra flatware row up top is a new feature for us that we are enjoying and still playing with. It's also convenient to have the ability to adjust the (formerly top rack) cup rack up and down etc. to help make all the things fit both above and below. This level also has a bottle blaster row that has larger prongs that have water jets in them to clean out your reusable bottles or those hard to reach locations. Super handy for those with kids or who like to use the reusable water bottles. It's SUPER SUPER quiet; I didn't measure against what GE states the decibel (db) level to be, but in my experience assisting in undersea acoustics in a past life, I believe this to be very close, if not quieter then the stated db level (I think their number was conservative). The bottom row has multiple adjustment points within the rack to change the configuration of the rows. I really like that feature as it changes how things fit - for the better! The instructions are extremely helpful in relaying all info, including the discrete details. As mentioned above I'm new to this and have never installed a DW! Small related sidebar - I read a review about this product where the person said after they installed it, that it was too loud. But I noted 2 locations in the instructions that called out specific steps to take to reduce noise levels and the reviewer in that instance stated they didn't complete one of the tasks. In that case it was user error, all they had to do was follow the well laid out instructions. That all to say, this puppy noise dampens well. I also like that it has a small convenience light on the front panel to indicate its status to you, so you know when it's running or complete - you're covered there too! I'm really enjoying the top buttons compared to the old front buttons. With the front buttons my kids press them because they make noise and light up, and so does my stomach or my belt, if I'm reaching for something in the cabinet etc. But with top buttons they are tucked up under the counter and even small wondering fingers can't make their way onto them (or my stomach)! In comparison to our old unit, this GE is night and day difference. And it brings a little peace of mind with the quality build and the GE name! A few improvements that could be made. Let's face it, what's an honest critique if we don't find something that can be done better? Something can ALWAYS be improved upon (the principal of continuous improvement)! Between the old unit and this one we lost some space inside for dishes and maybe silverware (yet to be seen as you can cover down on the new top row with some of the flatware). That removal of extra wash space however is likely what makes them more every efficient etc. I actually don't mind the loss of a small amount of the interior space as we tend to over pack these things anyway. I have no other suggested or recommended improvements and I have no other “complaints”. I installed the unit with no issue as a first timer and needed zero help. I am only slightly mechanically inclined and was able to do this all in about 4 hours start to finish. It's also a looker! Looks great in place, we selected the stainless steel and love the look. One thing I noted immediately was build quality in comparison to the rivals, who are typically electronics makers. Their construction didn't feel as solid or sturdy as the GE did. A few take always: The extra flatware row up top is a new feature for us that we are enjoying and still playing with. It's also convenient to have the ability to adjust the (formerly top rack) cup rack up and down etc. to help make all the things fit both above and below. This level also has a bottle blaster row that has larger prongs that have water jets in them to clean out your reusable bottles or those hard to reach locations. Super handy for those with kids or who like to use the reusable water bottles. It's SUPER SUPER quiet; I didn't measure against what GE states the decibel (db) level to be, but in my experience assisting in undersea acoustics in a past life, I believe this to be very close, if not quieter then the stated db level (I think their number was conservative). The bottom row has multiple adjustment points within the rack to change the configuration of the rows. I really like that feature as it changes how things fit - for the better! The instructions are extremely helpful in relaying all info, including the discrete details. As mentioned above I'm new to this and have never installed a DW! Small related sidebar - I read a review about this product where the person said after they installed it, that it was too loud. But I noted 2 locations in the instructions that called out specific steps to take to reduce noise levels and the reviewer in that instance stated they didn't complete one of the tasks. In that case it was user error, all they had to do was follow the well laid out instructions. That all to say, this puppy noise dampens well. I also like that it has a small convenience light on the front panel to indicate its status to you, so you know when it's running or complete - you're covered there too! I'm really enjoying the top buttons compared to the old front buttons. With the front buttons my kids press them because they make noise and light up, and so does my stomach or my belt, if I'm reaching for something in the cabinet etc. But with top buttons they are tucked up under the counter and even small wondering fingers can't make their way onto them (or my stomach)! In comparison to our old unit, this GE is night and day difference. And it brings a little peace of mind with the quality build and the GE name! A few improvements that could be made. Let's face it, what's an honest critique if we don't find something that can be done better? Something can ALWAYS be improved upon (the principal of continuous improvement)! Between the old unit and this one we lost some space inside for dishes and maybe silverware (yet to be seen as you can cover down on the new top row with some of the flatware). That removal of extra wash space however is likely what makes them more every efficient etc. I actually don't mind the loss of a small amount of the interior space as we tend to over pack these things anyway. I have no other suggested or recommended improvements and I have no other “complaints”. I installed the unit with no issue as a first timer and needed zero help. I am only slightly mechanically inclined and was able to do this all in about 4 hours start to finish. It's also a looker! Looks great in place, we selected the stainless steel and love the look. Picture included.

One thing I noted immediately was build quality in comparison to the rivals, who are typically electronics makers. Their construction didn't feel as solid or sturdy as the GE did. A few take always: The extra flatware row up top is a new feature for us that we are enjoying and still playing with. It's also convenient to have the ability to adjust the (formerly top rack) cup rack up and down etc. to help make all the things fit both above and below. This level also has a bottle blaster row that has larger prongs that have water jets in them to clean out your reusable bottles or those hard to reach locations. Super handy for those with kids or who like to use the reusable water bottles. It's SUPER SUPER quiet; I didn't measure against what GE states the decibel (db) level to be, but in my experience assisting in undersea acoustics in a past life, I believe this to be very close, if not quieter then the stated db level (I think their number was conservative). The bottom row has multiple adjustment points within the rack to change the configuration of the rows. I really like that feature as it changes how things fit - for the better! The instructions are extremely helpful in relaying all info, including the discrete details. As mentioned above I'm new to this and have never installed a DW! Small related sidebar - I read a review about this product where the person said after they installed it, that it was too loud. But I noted 2 locations in the instructions that called out specific steps to take to reduce noise levels and the reviewer in that instance stated they didn't complete one of the tasks. In that case it was user error, all they had to do was follow the well laid out instructions. That all to say, this puppy noise dampens well. I also like that it has a small convenience light on the front panel to indicate its status to you, so you know when it's running or complete - you're covered there too! I'm really enjoying the top buttons compared to the old front buttons. With the front buttons my kids press them because they make noise and light up, and so does my stomach or my belt, if I'm reaching for something in the cabinet etc. But with top buttons they are tucked up under the counter and even small wondering fingers can't make their way onto them (or my stomach)! In comparison to our old unit, this GE is night and day difference. And it brings a little peace of mind with the quality build and the GE name! A few improvements that could be made. Let's face it, what's an honest critique if we don't find something that can be done better? Something can ALWAYS be improved upon (the principal of continuous improvement)! Between the old unit and this one we lost some space inside for dishes and maybe silverware (yet to be seen as you can cover down on the new top row with some of the flatware). That removal of extra wash space however is likely what makes them more every efficient etc. I actually don't mind the loss of a small amount of the interior space as we tend to over pack these things anyway. I have no other suggested or recommended improvements and I have no other “complaints”. I installed the unit with no issue as a first timer and needed zero help. I am only slightly mechanically inclined and was able to do this all in about 4 hours start to finish. It's also a looker! Looks great in place, we selected the stainless steel and love the look. Picture included.

Sentence (English): I bought this a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Works Remarkably Well ] || ---------------- || I bought this a month ago. The dishes come out very clean (5 stars for that). I am using Kirkland dishwashing tablets from Costco. After using the regular wash cycle which takes about 2.5 hrs, the dishes come out wet with a lot of condensation of moisture everywhere -hence the ding in stars. It uses very low power (0.5KWh per wash which works to 15-20 cents). I found a workaround which is to use the extended heat option which takes an extra 15 min and the dishes come out clean, dry, and perfect -costs twice as much per use but is worth it. With this combo, it is the best washer ever. So I pick use regular wash with the Extended Dry option or Express wash which completes in 1 hr with the extended dry option. The machine itself is perfect. Whoever did the design for programming the cycles did not do a good job. Or it could be that they would not get the Energy star rating if they included the extended heat option as part of the regular wash cycle. Another plus for this machine is almost no noise when running the machine. The control placement is all good. Just wish it was more aesthetically pleasing -it looks like a machine from 20 years ago. Overall very satisfied with this purchase and you can't go wrong with this washer. Just hope it continues to work without any issues. Highly recommended for anyone in the market.

I suppose that's because the drum is plastic, so the interior doesn't stay hot very long. A technician came out to check it, and he said it's performing as it should then told me "builder-grade" appliances just don't perform very well. (I'm pretty sure he wasn't supposed to say that.) I love the placement of the silverware holder on the inside of the door. That leaves extra room for large items on the bottom shelf. I'm satisfied with the appliance, but I wouldn't buy this model again.

Reason for selection. : I'm the head of a one-person, two-cat household with two cats. Honestly, when I first started living alone, I dreamed of cooking while living alone, so I cooked a lot of things. But as most people who live alone know, the kitchen is really small. I can't cook anything fancy, and even if I do, there's no space, so I have to keep washing dishes and cleaning up while cooking. It was fun at first, but after a while, it became too much of a hassle, and cooking for myself didn't save that much money. I figured it would be more profitable to just buy fast food or something simple to eat and come home, so I stopped eating at home after that. But just because I don't eat at home doesn't mean there won't be dishes to wash. Especially because I have to wash the cats' water bowls, food bowls, and snack bowls. I have to wash those every day, so it's really annoying. Just the dishes we use at home are about 10 a day. I wash them in the morning and evening, and I do it every day before work and after work, so it's become a habit, but sometimes I think about buying a dishwasher. So I ended up ordering a dishwasher, but since I only needed to wash the cats' dishes, I felt like I didn't need something like a six-person dishwasher. I'd heard that a three-person dishwasher is small and won't fit large pots, but since I only need small dishes, this one was perfect! And my choice was right! It holds all the dishes without a hitch. 3. Detailed Review: At first, I was a little worried about the orange color. I don't think it's a particularly pretty color, so I was a little worried about the interior design. But after thinking about it, I realized my house was so dirty that I didn't need to worry about that. When I first got the call that the package had arrived, I was excited, thinking, "I'll go and take a picture!" But what the... why is the box so big? It was so big that it wouldn't fit through my front door. I had a cat door installed, so the width wasn't even a bit tight. So I ended up having to take the dishwasher outside and bring it inside. I was worried because it weighed 14kg, but it was really heavy. But a woman can lift it alone! My back hurts a little, but it's not so bad that I can't handle it. It was packaged so securely that it arrived without any damage. When I opened the dishwasher door, everything was right inside. I haven't had time to install it yet, so I haven't had a chance to properly inspect it, but it still has everything I need. There was even a dehumidifier on the bottom. At first, I thought it was a detergent, and I was a little impressed, but it turned out to be a disappointment. While the interior isn't particularly large, I think it'll fit small dishes, so I'm quite satisfied. While it's a hassle to wash and store the dishes, they dry out on their own once they're inside, so I'm diligently trying to wash them and put them away the next day. I'm a working adult, so I'm too tired to do everything during the week. I'll install it this weekend and write a more detailed review. 4. Conclusion: I was surprised by how much bigger it was! For those who live alone and don't necessarily cook at home often, and who don't mind washing large pots and pans when they do, but would prefer to at least wash the dishes, this would be a great option for households with pets. Steam sterilization, high-temperature washing at 72 degrees Celsius, and easy drying and storage functions make it even more useful. This is my review after trying it out for a while :). . Sentence (English): The machine is great and does a wonderful job.
Comments (English): [ Great machine….but! ] || ---------------- || The machine is great and does a wonderful job. It's quiet, looks fantastic and is full of features that I enjoy. BUT…. 1st, why not just a 'Dry touch-up' for after the 'Quick Wash'? Nobody likes wet dishes! 2ndly …this REALLY bothers me… the 'rack rollers' along with the racks themselves seem to be super flimsy and cheaply made. The whole racks wobble from side to side giving you the notion that you just paid top dollar for junk. $1500 for what seems like a throwaway product. 3rdly…. I really wish dishwasher manufacturers would make a more substantial 'track guide' for the bottom rack to keep it from coming off the track. Literally every dishwasher I've used over the last 10-15 years utilizes tiny wheels on what seems to be an after thought track system that makes it derail when fully loaded. My old KitchenAid from the 80's was amazing. Felt like a beast and performed like one too. Come to think of it…I miss it and it's well thought out design.

Actually, that might be my one complaint: it's hard to get the filter and stainless grate out to clean them because the spinning jets (? ) get in the way. The visual confirmation that the wash has ended also ensures that my kids can't say they didn't know they needed to unload the dishwasher! This is not the cheapest dishwasher out there, but it's worth the price. I've been really pleased with all my LG appliances; we have a refrigerator, washer, dryer, dishwasher, and even a TV and they have been excellent. Hope this helps you make a decision if you are like me and read the reviews obsessively before a major purchase!

Sentence (English): Purchased this item (Samsung Smart 42dBA Dishwasher with StormWash and SmartDry) in Dec 2022 and it lasted 2 months before it sprang a leak with enough water to soak through its enclosed cabinet.
Comments (English): Purchased this item (Samsung Smart 42dBA Dishwasher with StormWash and SmartDry) in Dec 2022 and it lasted 2 months before it sprang a leak with enough water to soak through its enclosed cabinet. But the problem with this dishwasher started from the its very first use. We ran it the night after the install and noticed that the water did not drain out completely after the cycle. Water had accumulated around the mesh strainer on the bottom. We removed the strainer to see if there was any blockage but did not find anything, just water like clogged drain. We discovered that it did not drain completely only when the cycle was set to 'Normal' and seemed to drain on other settings. So thought to ourselves that we'll just avoid the Normal cycle. Then we noticed that the noise was a lot louder than our old Maytag dishwasher; one of the reasons we purchased this Samsung dishwasher because of its 'whisper quiet' claim. Well, perhaps we'll get used to it, not like we ran it everyday anyway. But then when loading the dishwasher with two days worth of dishes (there are only two of us plus a cat in our household) it became perfectly clear that the rack design did not allow to fit two days worth of two sets of plates, bowls, cups, possibly quart size pan/pot with some pet dishes. And the third rack on top. utterly useless as it did nothing to clean spatulas or other utensils. We were becoming disillusioned fast with this dishwasher. Then finally one day after almost two months of putting up with its multiple shortcomings, it started to flash "LC" code. didn't need to look up what it was because the water had already spread across our kitchen floor. We've had few dishwashers through the years but none had ever sprang a leak on us before. One positive note in this exercise in frustration is that Costco was great and quick to process the returns. We purchased a GE dishwasher this time around and got it installed today. And even though the GE's decibel level is higher than the Samsung's "42dBA", it is running almost silently. Go figure. Chatted with the delivery/install people while the new dishwasher was being installed, they told us that they handle Samsung dishwasher returns most often. Wish we had that info before purchasing. well, but now you do.

Sentence (English): It has a large volume and gets dishes clean, the most important features for a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Gets dishes clean ] || ---------------- || It has a large volume and gets dishes clean, the most important features for a dishwasher. Really enjoy the third top rack for small, delicate, easy to loose things. The red light on the floor to indicate it is running is useful for those who did not start the machine. I also like the delay feature, which I use a lot. Would not buy a machine without it.However, the sleek design makes it hard to tell if I set the cycles right. If I open the door did I just mess up the setting? Do I need to reset, or not? After a few months I thought I got it down but still there are times it did not run overnight as expected. I thought I did the usual delay settings! The settings and the dishwasher itself need to be more interactive. If it just sits there, has the delay feature been engaged? Has it run? Especially for those who did not set the machine it is impossible to tell.

Sentence (English): Is it possible to be in love with an appliance?
Comments (English): [ Delightful dishwashing - for real! ] || ---------------- || Is it possible to be in love with an appliance? I (almost) look forward to doing the dishes because this machine is so pleasant to use. The stainless steel tub is a vast improvement over our 10+year old plastic tub dishwasher that you had to wash the dishes by hand before using. The tub looks perfect after 2 months of daily use. I mean, the dishwasher sends me a text (! ) when it's done via the ThinQ app. I can also track the number of cycles and be reminded to run maintenance cycles or clean the filter.Actually, that might be my one complaint: it's hard to get the filter and stainless grate out to clean them because the spinning jets (? ) get in the way. Maybe there is a way to move it and I've just been too lazy to look it up in the manual, so don't pay too much attention to this issue.I was won over by this model by the smooth gliding top rack; I don't know why it is so satisfying, but I love it! The visual confirmation that the wash has ended also ensures that my kids can't say they didn't know they needed to unload the dishwasher! This is not the cheapest dishwasher out there, but it's worth the price. I've been really pleased with all my LG appliances; we have a refrigerator, washer, dryer, dishwasher, and even a TV and they have been excellent. Hope this helps you make a decision if you are like me and read the reviews obsessively before a major purchase!

I would probably not buy the extendavent again, purely because we dont use it as much as we thought we would.

Sentence (English): We are a family of three who do not cook much at home.
Comments (English): [ I ignored it because it was small, but it unexpectedly became an essential item that I couldn't live without. ] || ---------------- || We are a family of three who do not cook much at home. I have wanted to buy a dishwasher for a long time, but the kitchen is too small and we do not cook a lot of food, so I could not bring in a dishwasher because of my husband's opposition. Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

I have wanted to buy a dishwasher for a long time, but the kitchen is too small and we do not cook a lot of food, so I could not bring in a dishwasher because of my husband's opposition. Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ I ignored it because it was small, but it unexpectedly became an essential item that I couldn't live without. ] || ---------------- || We are a family of three who do not cook much at home. I have wanted to buy a dishwasher for a long time, but the kitchen is too small and we do not cook a lot of food, so I could not bring in a dishwasher because of my husband's opposition. Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ I ignored it because it was small, but it unexpectedly became an essential item that I couldn't live without. ] || ---------------- || We are a family of three who do not cook much at home. I have wanted to buy a dishwasher for a long time, but the kitchen is too small and we do not cook a lot of food, so I could not bring in a dishwasher because of my husband's opposition. Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. I have wanted to buy a dishwasher for a long time, but the kitchen is too small and we do not cook a lot of food, so I could not bring in a dishwasher because of my husband's opposition. Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ I ignored it because it was small, but it unexpectedly became an essential item that I couldn't live without. ] || ---------------- || We are a family of three who do not cook much at home. I have wanted to buy a dishwasher for a long time, but the kitchen is too small and we do not cook a lot of food, so I could not bring in a dishwasher because of my husband's opposition. Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

Also, sadly, I cannot drill holes in the house. I cannot drill holes for water inlet and outlet, make holes, or do whatever I want with the kitchen cabinets. I think I could hardly even dream of installing a large dishwasher. Then, I found this dishwasher with a minimal size and got it. The criteria for the dishwasher I want are 1. It should be a minimal size that does not take up much space in the kitchen and should not be difficult to drill holes or install - It is really easy to install! Just place it in a horizontal place and put the drain hose in it and place it where it will drain. And it seems easier to just supply water myself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water is filled properly, it will beep and then you should stop the water supply immediately. 2. It is not difficult to use - After filling the water, add detergent and press the mode you want by hand to operate. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini size is big enough to fit the largest plate I use - We are a family of 3 and we do not eat a lot of food or eat often. So when cups or small dishes come out, it is good to wash them and put them away right away. The largest plate is a white flat IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it to the side. I think it might be a little difficult to use for people who use a lot of large plates. It is a good size to put in rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. It is a dishwasher that fits my lifestyle. If it is too big, it will not be done this quickly, and if you have to run a lot at once, it will be burdensome and the dishes will pile up. *** As I continued to use it, I realized that there are more minor disadvantages than I thought. 1. The process of adding water that requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews said that an error occurred, but I didn't know that I would be the one who would experience that error. The E4 error occurred! This is really important. They say that you should plug in the dishwasher cord and turn on the power button! Then, add water to avoid this error. I knew this in advance from the product review, so I thought I could use it with confidence. After my husband installed it, he just poured water without thinking and didn't turn on the power button. Then, when he turned on the power button, the E4 error occurred. I looked for a blog review, and it said to drain all the water, clean it thoroughly, and then use it again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and dried it thoroughly. I barely managed to use it after getting an error and drying it several times. Please read my review and keep in mind! You should always turn on the power before adding water. And if you hear a beep while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is really a sustress. 2. Drying and blowing function. This is the most disappointing feature, though. When the dishwasher is done washing, it seems to dry the dishes like a fine (?) wind. If you don't open the door, it will continue to blow and dry the dishes. The blowing function is so weak that I've never seen the dishes completely dry by the next day. So it dries better if you just leave the door open. The problem is that when you leave the door open, it gets in the way of going in and out because of the door. So I bought a safety device from Daiso to prevent the door from opening and closing, and I can keep it slightly open. The door is either completely closed or completely open, which is a polar opposite. There are some disappointing points, but I'm satisfied with the price. I always have to consider the price of home appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person anymore. If you think drying is important, you should look for other products with added functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a bit annoying to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else in filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.
